version.changelog:
**Major update: Migrated to OpenClaw runtime with trigger-based execution and environment-provided tool integration.**

- Added OpenClaw adapter and modular handler files for market monitoring and event processing.
- Introduced trigger handlers: monitorHandler (interval-based) and eventHandler (storage event-driven).
- All state persistence and market/order interactions now use OpenClaw tools via the adapter.
- Reorganized directory and component structure for clarity and separation of concerns.
- Removed direct Upbit API/signing logic; all authentication is managed by the environment.
- Enhanced reliability and safety controls through state-aware storage operations and tool-validated order checks.

llm.summary: The skill claims to run exclusively via OpenClaw tools without requiring credentials, but the repository also contains standalone worker scripts and an Upbit client that expect local API keys and filesystem I/O — these mismatches merit caution before installing or running.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description and SKILL.md describe an OpenClaw-hosted trading engine that uses injected tools for all I/O and says credentials are managed by the environment. However the repository also contains standalone worker scripts (eventWorker.js, monitor.js), an UpbitClient that performs JWT signing, and an env_example.txt with UPBIT_OPEN_API_ACCESS_KEY and UPBIT_OPEN_API_SECRET_KEY. Registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential — that contradicts the code. This implies the bundle supports both an OpenClaw handler mode and a local mode that requires direct API credentials and filesystem access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs handlers to use OpenClaw tools (storageGet/storageSet, placeOrder, getAccounts, etc.) and defines monitorHandler/eventHandler as triggers. That is scoped correctly for the declared purpose. However README and the included worker scripts give explicit instructions to run local Node processes that read .env and write/modify local resources/events.json and positions files; those steps are outside SKILL.md and expand the runtime surface (local I/O and direct API signing). The presence of both instruction sets grants broader behavior depending on how the code is run.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the registry (instruction-only). The package.json is present but lists no dependencies even though the code requires axios, jsonwebtoken, uuid, crypto (builtin), and dotenv — this is inconsistent and will cause runtime errors if someone follows the README and runs npm install expecting dependencies to be set. There are no external download URLs or archive extracts. Risk is moderate due to missing dependency declarations and divergent run modes rather than remote-install injection.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata declares no required env vars, but env_example.txt and the worker scripts clearly expect UPBIT_OPEN_API_ACCESS_KEY and UPBIT_OPEN_API_SECRET_KEY. SKILL.md asserts 'Tool-Auth: Credentials (API Keys) are managed by the OpenClaw environment' and the handler implementations use an OpenClawAdapter; nonetheless, local worker scripts bypass this and read .env directly. Requiring full Upbit API keys is proportionate for trading, but the discrepancy between declared requirements and actual code is concerning because a user may inadvertently supply secrets to a runtime mode not governed by the platform's tooling.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and uses OpenClaw storage APIs for state when run in handler mode. However the repository includes local scripts that read/write resources/events.json and similar files on disk when run outside OpenClaw. That local persistence is less privileged than system-wide changes but can cause secrets to be stored on disk (.env) or leak through backups/logs if run locally. The skill does not appear to modify other skills or system agent configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package is inconsistent: the SKILL.md and handlers are implemented to run inside OpenClaw using injected tools (and in that mode you don't hand the skill your Upbit keys), but the repo also contains standalone worker scripts and an UpbitClient that expect a local .env with your Upbit API keys and write to resources/*.json. Before installing or running:

- Decide whether you will run this inside OpenClaw or locally. If inside OpenClaw, confirm the platform's tools are used (monitorHandler/eventHandler) and ignore/remove local worker scripts if possible.
- Do not paste your Upbit API keys into .env or into the platform unless you trust the execution environment. If you must run locally, keep keys in a secure secret store and avoid committing .env to source control.
- The package.json does not declare dependencies (axios, jsonwebtoken, uuid are used but not listed). Running npm install as-is may not install required libs—review and fix package.json before running local scripts.
- Inspect and test event handling and persistence logic in a safe test account (or Upbit testnet if available) — the code will place live orders in local mode.
- If you plan to use this on OpenClaw, verify the platform actually provides the exact tools expected by openclawAdapter (getMarkets, getCandles, placeOrder, storageGet, storageSet, getAccounts, getOrdersChance, etc.) and that the handlers configured in SKILL.md are the ones that will be executed. 

Given the mismatches between declared requirements and code, treat this skill as suspicious until you confirm which runtime mode will be used and audit the code path that will receive your credentials.
